tagline.text: A protected area in the hills of Ilagan with caves and a tree-top adventure

location.label: Location
location.text: Barangay Santa Victoria, Ilagan City, Isabela (about 9.3 km from Ilagan town)

best_season.label: Best time to visit
best_season.text: November–May dry season (best for caves and walks)

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱500–1,500 (day trip from Cauayan or Ilagan; admission, transport and meals, estimated)

airport.label: Nearest airport
airport.text: Cauayan Airport (CYZ) or Ninoy Aquino International Airport, Manila (MNL), then overland

children.text: Fuyot Springs National Park is an 819-hectare protected area on the slopes of Santa Victoria in Ilagan City, Isabela. Inside it, the Ilagan Sanctuary offers caves, a canopy bridge walk above the forest, a zipline and a mini zoo, making it a good place for a family trip and light adventure in one stop.

Fuyot Springs National Park is a protected area on the mountain slopes of Barangay Santa Victoria in Ilagan City, Isabela. According to Wikipedia, it covers 819 hectares, was established by Proclamation No. 327 on October 8, 1938, and lies about
405 km

northeast of Manila. It falls under IUCN Category V (protected landscape) and is co-managed by the Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR) and the Ilagan city government. The park is said to extend into the neighboring Tumauini area and is known for mountain trails, caves, unusual rock formations, natural springs and Pinzal Falls.

The park's history goes back to the Commonwealth period. Proclamation No. 327 (October 8, 1938), signed by President Manuel L. Quezon, set aside land in Ilagan as a park "for the benefit and enjoyment of the people of the Philippines" under Act No. 3915, the law providing for national parks and game refuges. The land was withdrawn from sale, settlement and other disposition, subject to existing private rights, and its boundaries are shown on Bureau of Forestry map N.P.-26. At that time it was managed by the Bureau of Forestry.

What most travelers actually visit is the Ilagan Sanctuary (ILAGAN Sanctuary) inside the park. The city tourism page describes it as an animal, garden and nature sanctuary of about 200 hectares. According to one blog, caves make up about 25% of the park's 819 hectares. Inside the sanctuary there are a zipline, a tree-top adventure, horseback riding, a cable car, crystal-clear pools and a lagoon, Imusok Cave, flower gardens and picnic areas, as well as viewpoints and prayer spots such as Prayer Mountain and Calvary Hills. For families there are go-karts, ATV rides, a mini train, a zoo and aviary, a fishpond and a playground.
Ilagan City is about
from Manila by road, roughly
8 hours
by car, and about
1 hour
from Cauayan City. One blog says the sanctuary is
9.3 km

from Ilagan town. It is one of Isabela's leading family outings and also a DENR protected area. The park's legal status and management keep changing. Senate documents mention a bill to declare it an ecotourism destination and a Protected Area Management Board, and in April 2022 the Manila Times reported that DENR's Cagayan Valley office had monitored improvements to ecotourism facilities in the park. Which facilities are open now can change from time to time, so check with the city tourism office before you go.

According to one blog, this is a nine-chambered cave system said to be about 400 m long (no official figure was found), with more than 12 limestone caves. Four Class III caves are open to the public, and they are said to be relatively safe for beginners. A guide is required.
About 89 m long with three chambers, it is the largest of the Class III caves open for exploration. You can see calcite clusters, flowstone and columns.

Moon Cave has an opening in the middle that lets light in. Altar Cave is about 69 m long and has an altar-shaped fissure. Adventure Cave is more difficult and meant for experienced visitors. Fruit bats live in the caves, so flash photography is prohibited.

A canopy walk of seven wooden hanging bridges about 30 m (about 100 ft) above the ground, linking platforms built around native trees. It suits visitors comfortable with heights and gives you a view of the forest from above.

According to Wikipedia and a travel guide, there is a 350 m zipline, which is reported to have opened in May 2012 during Ilagan's 326th founding anniversary celebration. The sanctuary is also said to have a cable car with panoramic views. Check operating hours on site.
There is a mini zoo, an aviary and a butterfly park, which are good for children. Wikipedia also mentions a natural spring pool and ATV rides.
Prayer Mountain has a pavilion and a golf cart service to the trailhead, and offers good views. Together with Calvary Hills, it is known as a place for quiet prayer and rest.

The city tourism page describes clear pools, a serene lagoon, Imusok Cave, lush rainforest, flower gardens and picnic areas. It is a relaxing space that is worth more than just the caves and the canopy bridges. Horseback riding on hidden trails is also offered, so allow plenty of time if you are spending the day.
Arrive at the sanctuary from Ilagan town by tricycle or vehicle, buy your ticket and be assigned a guide.
Explore Main Cave, Moon Cave and Altar Cave in turn with your guide. Bats live here, so keep the flash off.
Have lunch at the on-site restaurant or a picnic area.
Cross the Tree Top Adventure bridges and look down on the forest.
Enjoy the view and rest at Prayer Mountain or Calvary Hills.
One blog says it is open until 10 PM from Friday to Sunday, but another guide (2025) lists 8 AM-5 PM daily, so sources disagree. Do not count on an evening visit and confirm the hours beforehand.
Explore the caves, then see the zoo and butterfly park.
Eat at the on-site restaurant and rest.
Choose the activities you want, such as the zipline, cable car, go-karts or ATV.
Watch the sunset from Prayer Mountain, then return to town.
No official information on activity prices could be found, so check at the entrance.
Manila to Ilagan is about
by road, roughly
8 hours
by car. Take a long-distance bus toward Isabela and get off at Ilagan. No confirmed information on exact fares and times is available, so check at the terminal.
One source gives about 405 km northeast of Manila for the park, so distinguish between straight-line distance and road distance.

items.title: From Ilagan town to the park

children.text: Take a northbound bus, jeepney or van, get off at the junction to the park, and take a tricycle to the sanctuary. The sanctuary is about
9.3 km
from Ilagan town.
One listing gives the address of the Sta. Victoria Caves as the National Highway, Barangay San Andres, Ilagan. Tell the tricycle driver "Ilagan Sanctuary" or "Sta. Victoria Caves."

items.title: From Cauayan and other Isabela cities

children.text: It is about
from Cauayan City to Ilagan City, roughly
1 hour
by car. If you arrive at Cauayan Airport (CYZ), use this route.
If you combine it with the dam or other Isabela sights, chartering a vehicle is convenient.

Cave exploration can be uncomfortable when it rains heavily, so the November–May dry season is best. It is hot in Isabela from March to May, so plan caves in the morning and the cooler forest bridges in the afternoon.

Hours differ by source and cannot be pinned down. One blog (May 2024) gives 8 AM–6 PM Monday to Thursday and 8 AM–10 PM Friday to Sunday, while another guide (2025) says 8 AM–5 PM daily, so plan on a closing time of about 5–6 PM, go early, and ask the City Tourism Office whether weekend evening hours really exist. In the rainy season, cave entrances are slippery and the site may close in heavy rain, so check the weather too. Weekdays tend to be quieter, while weekends and holidays can be crowded with families.

The city tourism page says the sanctuary has couple cottages, a canteen, ample parking and clean restrooms. Specific room rates have not been confirmed, so inquire before booking. Most visitors stay in Ilagan town or Cauayan City and make a day trip. The sanctuary also reportedly has a golf cart service, a cable car station, a climbing wall and a convention hall, so if you are visiting as a group or for an event, ask in advance whether facilities are available.

You can buy snacks inside the park and there are picnic areas, so you can also bring a packed lunch. For restaurants, choose in Ilagan town. No specific restaurant names could be confirmed, so none are listed.
A licensed guide is required for cave exploration, so be assigned one on site.
The caves are a fruit bat habitat, so do not use flash and move quietly.
In some sections it is easy to bump your head, so wear a helmet or hat and move slowly.
The Tree Top Adventure can be hard if you fear heights, so decide according to how you feel.
Bring non-slip shoes and a change of clothes. The cave floor may be wet.
You can ask the City Tourism Office (078 624 1511) and the Ilagan tourist information center (078 324 7769) about rates and hours in advance.
Bring plenty of cash. Activities may be paid for separately.
Before starting the cave tour, confirm the route included (which caves) and the time with your guide; it makes planning easier.
Fuyot Springs National Park is a protected area, so follow the rules and do not damage the caves or forest. Rates and facility operations change from time to time.
Some travel sites wrongly place the park in Baggao, Cagayan. It is in Barangay Santa Victoria, Ilagan City, Isabela.
No official rate table could be found. The admission fees come from a blog (May 2024), and activity prices could not be confirmed, so check on site.
The caves and bridges have safety rules, so follow the instructions of guides and staff.
In the rainy season the cave floors are slippery, and operations may stop in heavy rain.
The park is one of Isabela's leading protected areas, but it is not the much larger Northern Sierra Madre Natural Park. Do not confuse them.
A large multipurpose dam in Ramon, Isabela. It is about an hour and a half by car from Ilagan, so it can be combined in a regional itinerary.
The Philippines' largest protected area, in eastern Isabela. Fuyot Springs is described as a neighboring protected area.
One of Isabela's main cities, about 35.5 km from Ilagan; a good place to find lodging and restaurants.
The World Heritage rice terraces of Ifugao. They can be part of a northern Luzon loop linking Isabela and Ifugao.
